p:cNvPr.descr: An image depicting a postulated mechanism for the reaction catalyzed by methylmalonyl-CoA mutase and several other coenzyme B12-dependent transformations. For the most part, this image is a circle of arrows pointing right and around. Each step sits on an arrow. Step 1: The Co—C bond undergoes hemolytic cleavage, yielding CO2+ and the 5’-deoxyadenosyl free radical. This arrow points to the 5’-deoxyadenosyl free radical, where C bonds left and right to H (both pink) and up to deoxyadenosine (in a box). Below C is a red dot and a rectangle with an N in each corner. Inside the box are pink arrows pointing from each N to Co2+ in the middle. Step 2: The radical is converted to 5’-deoxyadenosine by abstraction of a hydrogen atom from the substrate, producing a substrate radical. To the left of this arrow, inside the circle, is a substrate where C bonds left and up to nothing, down to H (in pink), and right to C. bonds up and right to nothing, and down to X (in blue). This arrow points to deoxyadenosine (in a box) bonds down to C, which bonds left, right, and down to H (in pink). This also has the same box with Ns in the corner as described above below it. To the right is a substrate radical, which is the same as described above, except the first C does not bond to a pink H; instead, it has one pink dot underneath C. Below this is an arrow, identified as radical rearrangement. This is step 3: The substrate radical is rearranged, producing a new radical with the carbon skeleton of the product. For methylmalonyl-CoA mutase, the migrating group (X) is –CO--S-CoA. This arrow points to C, which bonds right, left, and down to H (in pink), and up to deoxyadenosine (in a box). Below this is the same box with Ns as described above. To the right is a product like radical, where C bonds up and left to nothing, down to X (in blue) and right to C, which bonds up and right to nothing, and has a pink dot below C. Next, is an arrow, which has another arrow darting off, pointing to the product where C bonds left and up to nothing, down to X (in blue), and right to C. C bonds up and right to nothing, and down to H (in pink). This is step 4: A hydrogen from the 5’—CH3 of the deoxyadenosine is returned to the product like radical, forming product. The arrow points to C bonding right and left to H (in pink), up to deoxyadenosine (in a box), and has one pink dot below C. The same box with Ns, as described above, is below this. An arrow follows this, which is step 5: The bond between the 5’—CH2 of the deoxyadenosyl radical and cobalt is re-formed, regenerating the B12 cofactor in its stable CO3+ form, ready to undergo another reaction. The arrow points to coenzyme B12, where CH2 (H2 in pink) bonds up to deoxyadenosine and down to the same box with Ns, as described above, except CO3+ is in the middle, rather than CO2+. The next arrow is step 1, which begins the process all over.
